findings.issue: ApplyAsync mutates the TRACKED correspondence row inside the loop (Write(row, ...)) before it knows the whole batch is valid. If a later change throws — ParseDate on a malformed date, ParseConfidentiality on an unknown value, or the subject-cleared refusal inside Write — the earlier fields have already been written onto the tracked entity and are left Modified in the ChangeTracker, while no corrections row is created and the method throws. WakeelDb is scoped to the whole user session (see the AddWakeelCore comment: «a scope in الوكيل is the user's session»), so the very next SaveChangesAsync anywhere in that session (a notification, a follow-up, a status change) silently commits the half-applied edit to a NUMBERED correspondence item with no corrections record and no audit row — exactly the silent edit AGREEMENT item 19 forbids. Reachable from W25, whose own code comment notes that «every W25 field is posted together»: a user who fixes the subject and mistypes the date in the same submit loses the audit trail for the subject. The existing test A_field_that_may_not_be_corrected_is_refused_and_nothing_is_written passes only because it sends a single change that fails on the whitelist check before any Write.
findings.fix: Split validation from mutation: run the whole loop first in a read-only pass (whitelist check, Read(old), Normalize, skip no-ops, and PARSE the new value into its typed form without assigning it) building a list of (field, old, newText, parsedValue); throw before touching the row if anything is refused, and only then assign every parsed value to the row. Alternatively wrap the loop in try/catch and, on any exception, call await db.Entry(row).ReloadAsync(cancellationToken) before rethrowing so the context is left in step with the database. Add a test: ApplyAsync(approved.Id, [subject→"جديد", externalDate→"ليس تاريخًا"], reason) must throw, and after a subsequent unrelated SaveChanges the stored Subject must still be the original one and Corrections must be empty.

findings.issue: SameParty only compares PartyId and UnitId: `(candidate.PartyId is {} party && row.PartyId == party) || (candidate.UnitId is {} unit && row.UnitId == unit)`. When the counterparty is a typed name (PartyId and UnitId both null — a legal and, per CorrespondenceWorld.IncomingInput's own default, the ordinary path for a body not yet in the directory, since Validate accepts PartyNameSnapshot alone as a recipient), SameParty is false for every row. Registering the very same incoming letter twice from the same typed party with the same external number is therefore NOT blocked as an exact duplicate (B3-1: «تطابق دقيق (رقم الجهة + الجهة) يُمنع»); worse, it is surfaced with the factually wrong Arabic reason «الرقم نفسه مسجَّل لجهة أخرى» when it is in fact the same party. Both stored rows also get a second incoming official number for one letter.
findings.fix: Carry the typed name in DuplicateCandidate (add `string? PartyNameSnapshot`, filled from row.PartyNameSnapshot in CorrespondenceService.Candidate) and extend SameParty with a third arm: when the candidate has neither PartyId nor UnitId, compare ArabicText.Normalize(candidate.PartyNameSnapshot) with ArabicText.Normalize(row.PartyNameSnapshot) and treat a non-empty equal pair as the same party. Keep the id comparisons first so a directory party still wins. Add a test registering world.IncomingInput() (the typed-name default) twice with the same externalNumber and asserting CoreAr.CorrDuplicateExact plus an unchanged incoming sequence.

findings.issue: ImportAsync calls correspondence.CreateDraftAsync (which Adds the row and SaveChangesAsync — the draft is committed) and only then calls RegisterIncomingAsync. If registration refuses — an exact duplicate against a letter that was registered by hand, a clock verdict that is not Ok, a field check such as a future ExternalDate coming from the sender's NumberIssuedAt, or an OfficialNumberConcurrencyException — the exception propagates and a stray unnumbered incoming draft is left behind in the correspondence list with no way for the user to know where it came from. The two writes are not atomic and the caller cannot undo the first.
findings.fix: Wrap the create+register pair so a failed registration leaves nothing: either open one transaction around both (BeginTransactionAsync before CreateDraftAsync, commit after RegisterIncomingAsync, rollback + detach on failure, mirroring CorrespondenceService.RollbackAsync), or catch around RegisterIncomingAsync and call correspondence.DeleteDraftAsync(draft.Id, now) before rethrowing. Add a test that imports a package whose letter collides with an already-registered incoming (same external number and party) and asserts the exception plus Assert.Empty on the resulting drafts.

findings.issue: IFollowUpService.RunDueRemindersAsync is implemented, idempotent and tested, but nothing ever calls it: grep over src/ shows the only reference to IFollowUpService outside its own file is the DI registration, and ReminderScheduler.RunOnceAsync (the minute pass that raises meeting, appointment, task, commitment, cycle and backup reminders) has no correspondence-follow-up block. A follow-up reminder is therefore stored and never rings, so the spec's «متابعات … تذكير» is not delivered end-to-end.
findings.fix: Add one correspondence-follow-up pass to ReminderScheduler.RunOnceAsync, next to the existing ones, reading followups whose reminder_at falls in [from, utcNow] for correspondence still in New/InProgress/AwaitingReply and calling the existing RaiseAsync(ReminderScheduler.Key(FollowUpService.ReminderKeyKind, followup.Id, followup.ReminderAt.Value), FollowUpService.ReminderKind, CoreAr.CorrFollowupReminderTitle, CoreAr.CorrFollowupReminderBody(subject), CorrespondenceService.AuditEntityType, followup.CorrespondenceId, followup.ReminderAt) — that reuses the pass's single preloaded key set instead of the per-entry AnyAsync FollowUpService does today. ReminderScheduler.cs is outside the B3 package's paths and is currently modified by another agent, so this needs to be assigned to whoever owns that file; until it lands, the reminder half of FollowUpService is dead code.

findings.issue: CorrectionView/CorrectionEntry are the only view models in the package that are not Arabic-ready, breaking the package's own rule that «screens must never map an enum to a word of their own» (ARCHITECTURE §12, AGREEMENT item 15). Field is an English key ("externalNumber", "bodyText") with no Arabic label; Read() serialises Confidentiality as the English enum name ("Secret", "TopSecret"); Iso() serialises dates as "2026-09-16T00:00:00Z". The W25/log tab renders Changes directly, so the user would read English identifiers and ISO timestamps inside an Arabic record of what was corrected.
findings.fix: Add a CoreAr map for the correctable field labels (e.g. CorrFieldSubject = «الموضوع», CorrFieldExternalNumber = «رقم الجهة», …) and extend CorrectionEntry (or CorrectionView) with FieldLabelAr plus OldAr/NewAr computed at read time: run Confidentiality through CorrespondenceAr.Confidentiality and dates through the same Arabic date formatting the rest of the package uses, while keeping the raw Old/New strings stored in corrections.changes exactly as they are today so nothing about the stored record changes.

findings.issue: CorrCorrectionFieldUnknown(string field) => $"الحقل «{field}» لا يقبل التصحيح" interpolates the raw ENGLISH field identifier into an Arabic sentence the user reads ("الحقل «externalDate» لا يقبل التصحيح") — a technical term in user text (AGREEMENT item 15) and an unisolated Latin run inside an Arabic sentence (item 55, since the value is baked into the string before any bdi wrapper can reach it). CorrectionService also reuses this same sentence for two unrelated failures in ParseDate and ParseConfidentiality, where the field IS correctable and the real problem is an unreadable value — so the user is told the wrong thing.
findings.fix: Take an Arabic label rather than the key: CorrCorrectionFieldUnknown(string fieldLabelAr) fed from the CoreAr field-label map proposed above (callers pass CorrectionAr.FieldLabel(change.Field), falling back to a generic «هذا الحقل لا يقبل التصحيح» for an unrecognised key). Add separate strings for the value failures, e.g. CorrCorrectionBadDate = «تاريخ غير مقروء؛ أعد كتابته» and CorrCorrectionBadConfidentiality = «درجة سرية غير معروفة», and use those in ParseDate/ParseConfidentiality.

findings.issue: CancelAsync refuses an unnumbered item with CoreAr.CorrRefusedNotDraft = «هذه المراسلة لم تعد مسودة», but that branch is reached precisely because the item IS still an unnumbered draft. The user is told the opposite of the truth and is not pointed at the command that does apply (delete).
findings.fix: Add a dedicated string, e.g. CorrRefusedCancelDraft = «المسودة غير المرقّمة تُحذف ولا تُلغى», and throw that instead in the `row.OfficialNumber is null` branch of CancelAsync.

findings.issue: SetRecipientOnlyAsync and SetLinksAsync are the only state-changing commands in the package that write no audit_log row. «للمستلم فقط» is a distribution restriction (AGREEMENT item 7) that decides whether a letter leaves this installation in a sync package; turning it off is a security-relevant act and leaves no trace of who did it or when.
findings.fix: Call LogAsync from both, with new CoreAr summaries, e.g. CorrAuditRecipientOnlySet = «جُعلت المراسلة للمستلم فقط» / CorrAuditRecipientOnlyCleared = «رُفعت قيدة «للمستلم فقط»» and CorrAuditLinksChanged = «حُدّثت ارتباطات المراسلة»; assert the row in a test the way Every_transition_writes_one_audit_row already does.

findings.issue: ExportAsync only checks `row.OfficialNumber is null || row.ApprovedAt is null`, so an outgoing letter that was approved and later CANCELLED (AGREEMENT item 19: the number stays, the letter was withdrawn) can still be exported and delivered as a live .wakeel-msg. The receiving office would register a withdrawn letter as a normal incoming.
findings.fix: Add `|| row.Status == CorrespondenceStatus.Cancelled` to the refusal (a new CoreAr string, e.g. CorrExchangeCancelled = «المراسلة ملغاة؛ لا تُرسل»), and cover it with a test that approves, cancels and then expects the refusal.

findings.issue: For a package from another organisation the certificate chain is deliberately not verified (there is no shared root — this is inherent to AGREEMENT item 22), yet the preview still reports SignatureOk = true with CoreAr.CorrExchangeSignatureOk = «التوقيع سليم» and prints FromAr from self-asserted manifest fields. Anyone can mint a self-signed device certificate naming any organisation, so «التوقيع سليم» overstates what was actually proven; only «وارد خارجي» hints at the difference.
findings.fix: Differentiate the wording for the external case, e.g. a new CoreAr.CorrExchangeSignatureExternal = «التوقيع متماسك، لكن الجهة المرسِلة غير موثّقة لدينا» returned when !IsInternal, keeping «التوقيع سليم» for a package whose chain was actually checked against the pinned organisation key.

findings.issue: RunDueRemindersAsync loads EVERY open correspondence row (New/InProgress/AwaitingReply, id + subject) on every pass, even when only one follow-up is due, and then does one AnyAsync against notifications per due entry. Once the pass is wired to the minute tick this is a full scan of the open work of the office, every minute, forever.
findings.fix: Narrow the second read to the ids actually due — `var ids = due.Select(d => d.CorrespondenceId).Distinct().ToList(); ... .Where(c => ids.Contains(c.Id) && open states)` — and load the used reminder keys once with a single StartsWith(ReminderScheduler.KeyPrefix) query instead of one AnyAsync per entry (this falls out naturally if the pass is folded into ReminderScheduler.RunOnceAsync as finding 4 proposes).

findings.issue: The migration is technically right — ARCHITECTURE §5's two independent sequences make the first incoming and the first outgoing letter of the same day on the same device produce the identical text YYYYMMDD/DESSS, so 0001's global UNIQUE(official_number) made an ordinary pair impossible — but DATA-MODEL §0 line 23 names `correspondence.official_number` explicitly as one of the unfiltered unique indexes on official identifiers, and that sentence now describes an index that no longer exists under that name. The doc and the schema disagree.
findings.fix: No code change: the composite UNIQUE(direction, official_number) is the correct reading of ARCHITECTURE §5 and the «never filtered on deleted_at» policy is preserved (SchemaTests still asserts it under the new name). Ask the schema/docs owner to amend DATA-MODEL §0 to «(direction, official_number)» and confirm the rename for installations that already applied 0001 (DROP INDEX IF EXISTS handles them).

missing_spec_items: «متابعات … تذكير» — FollowUpService.RunDueRemindersAsync is written, idempotent and tested but is never invoked: ReminderScheduler.RunOnceAsync has no follow-up pass and nothing else calls it, so a follow-up reminder is stored and never rings. One call in ReminderScheduler (a file outside this package's paths, currently modified by another agent) completes it.

«تطابق دقيق (رقم الجهة + الجهة) يُمنع» is only enforced when the party is a directory party or an org unit; with a typed party name (the default data-entry path for a body not yet in the directory) the exact match never fires and the same letter can be registered twice, each time consuming an incoming number. See the DuplicateDetector finding.

«حذف المسودة غير المرقّمة نهائيًا» (AGREEMENT item 19) is implemented as a SOFT delete. The builder's reasoning is sound and documented in code (DATA-MODEL §0 forbids physically deleting a synced row, correspondence has only AFTER INSERT/UPDATE change_log triggers, so a physical DELETE would never reach the other devices and the draft would come back on the next sync), and the user experience is indistinguishable (global query filter hides it everywhere, no command restores it). It nonetheless deviates from the literal wording and needs the owner's ratification, or a schema change (AFTER DELETE trigger + a sync rule) if a true physical delete is wanted.

Out of scope by design, confirmed not silently dropped: TemplateService / LetterComposer / the OpenXML implementation of IDerivedDocumentBuilder (interface correctly defined here, implementation is the next package); VaultStore reading/writing the exchange attachments and calling LinkDocumentAsync (B3-2 — attachments are passed in and handed back as bytes, which is the right seam); the sync-export filter that acts on «للمستلم فقط» (the flag is stored, settable and returned; the filter belongs to the sync package).
notes:
Ran exactly `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Core` (Build succeeded, 0 Warnings, 0 Errors — TreatWarningsAsErrors is on) and `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests` (Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 449, Skipped: 0, Total: 449, 22 s). No file was modified by this review.

WHAT IS SOLID. The security-critical parts hold up. Numbering: `numbers.IssueAsync` has exactly two call sites in the whole solution, both inside `await using var transaction = await db.Database.BeginTransactionAsync(...)`, both preceded by EnsureUnnumberedDraft, and OfficialNumberService itself refuses to run without an open transaction — a draft can never be numbered. The rollback path is genuinely tested: ThrowAfterNumberingDetector throws inside the transaction right after the number is issued, and the test proves the sequence stays at 0 and the NEXT registration still gets 001 (CorrespondenceService.RollbackAsync detaches Added entries and reloads the rest, which is what keeps official_numbers from silently skipping). Clock: both numbering paths run the ARCHITECTURE §9 check themselves and turn a bad verdict into «لن تُصدر أرقام رسمية حتى التصحيح» instead of the numbering service's English contract message. Cancellation keeps the number, stores the trimmed reason, refuses an empty one, and writes both an audit row and a Status followup. Every transition is audited (ChangeStatusAsync, Cancel, Close, Archive, and FollowUpService.AddAsync when it carries statusTo). The state machine matches the spec exactly, including Draft→New only through registration/approval, free movement among the three working states, reopening Done/Closed into InProgress, Cancelled→Archived only, Archived terminal, and same-to-same refused.

EXCHANGE. The two-pass container open is correct and I verified it against Wakeel.Crypto rather than taking the comment on trust: ContainerReader verifies the producer's signature over the manifest regardless of VerifyCertificateChain, so the first probe open (chain off, only to read the producer org id) proves nothing it should not, and the second open turns the chain check on against the pinned org key when the producer claims our organisation — a forged "internal" package fails there and lands in the catch as «التوقيع غير سليم؛ لا تسجّل هذا الملف». The content key is sealed to the recipient X25519 key (ContainerKeySource.SealFor) with the org recovery copy in the manifest (item 17); DeviceIdentity and DeviceCertificate are supplied by the caller and never stored, and nothing key-shaped reaches the database, a log or an audit summary. I also checked the attachment-name path-traversal angle I expected to find: it is already closed upstream — ContainerReader.ValidateManifest runs every entry name through ContainerEntrySource.IsAcceptableName (rejects "..", rooted paths, invalid segment chars, reserved device names) before any byte is decrypted, so `name[AttachmentPrefix.Length..]` cannot produce a traversal. No finding there.

TESTS are real behaviour, not tautologies, and none of them skip. The exchange round trip runs two separate temporary installations with real certificates and real containers (the recipient numbers the letter on ITS own incoming sequence 20260916/22001 while the sender's number becomes external_number, and the preview is proven to write nothing with Assert.Empty(recipient.Db.Correspondence)). The Arabic duplicate tests use genuine office subjects with tashkeel, tatweel, ه for ة and ى for ي, and include a case pinned exactly at the 0.8 boundary (4 shared words of a 5-word union) and a negative case. An_overdue_awaiting_reply_reaches_the_attention_center_and_the_correspondence_badge covers the attention/badge requirement; AttentionService already reads New/InProgress/AwaitingReply and BadgeService maps CorrespondenceIn/Out onto the correspondence badge, and FollowUpService.AddAsync keeps correspondence.due_at in step with the agreed next date, so the counts do pick the new states up.

ARABIC/RTL. All new user text is Arabic with no technical terms and no error codes, and CorrespondenceRefusedException carries a finished sentence the screen shows directly. Embedding values (numbers, subjects) into CoreAr sentences without Unicode isolation follows the established repo convention — the UI wraps them in bdi — so I did not flag it; the one genuine violation is the English field identifier baked into CorrCorrectionFieldUnknown (reported).

WHY 'fix' RATHER THAN 'accept'. One high and five medium findings. The high one is the only defect I would call dangerous: a multi-field correction that fails part way leaves the already-written fields Modified on a session-lifetime DbContext, so an unrecorded edit to a NUMBERED letter gets committed by the next unrelated SaveChanges — the exact silent edit item 19 exists to prevent, and it is reachable from W25's post-all-fields form. The rest are contained: the typed-name duplicate gap (also the wrong Arabic reason on the most common data-entry path), the orphan draft a failed import leaves behind, the reminder pass nobody calls, and the two Arabic-readiness gaps in the correction view and its refusal wording. None of them requires rework of the design — the shape of the package is right and I would not ask for anything to be rewritten.

ONE COORDINATION ITEM for the supervisor: finding 4's fix is a single call inside ReminderScheduler.RunOnceAsync, which is outside this package's allowed paths and is being edited by another agent right now (it shows as modified in git status). It needs to be handed to whoever owns that file, or explicitly granted to the B3 builder, or the follow-up reminder stays dead code. Finding 12 (the 0003 index rename versus DATA-MODEL §0's literal wording) is a docs decision for the owner, not a code change — the migration itself is right.
